16	package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.service;
17	
18	import java.util.Locale;
19	
20	import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.LocalityResolver;
21	import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.util.Sha256;
22	import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
23	
24	/**
25	 * Builds an owner's {@code customerCode}, formatted {@code <REGION>-<HASH8>} where REGION is the
26	 * canonical region derived from the owner's postcode and HASH8 is the first eight upper-case hex
27	 * characters of the SHA-256 of the owner's normalized telephone concatenated with the last name
28	 * (e.g. {@code "NSW-1A2B3C4D"}).
29	 */
30	@Component
31	public class CustomerCodeGenerator {
32	
33	    /** Number of leading hex characters of the SHA-256 digest kept as the identity hash. */
34	    private static final int HASH_LENGTH = 8;
35	
36	    /**
37	     * Build the customer code for the given postcode, normalized telephone and last name.
38	     *
39	     * @param postcode            the owner's postcode; its region forms the leading segment
40	     * @param normalizedTelephone the owner's telephone in canonical (E.164) form; hashed with the
41	     *                            last name to form the trailing segment
42	     * @param lastName            the owner's last name; hashed with the telephone
43	     * @return the formatted customer code
44	     */
45	    public String generate(String postcode, String normalizedTelephone, String lastName) {
46	        String region = LocalityResolver.resolveFromPostcode(postcode);
47	        String hash = Sha256.hex(normalizedTelephone + lastName)
48	            .substring(0, HASH_LENGTH).toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
49	        return region + "-" + hash;
50	    }
51	}

A household groups owners 25 * that share the same last name and postcode; this component normalizes the last name (so 26 * values differing only in casing or spacing are treated as equal) and derives a stable, 27 * shared {@code householdId} from the normalized last name and the postcode. 28 * 29 *

The id is deterministic: the same (last name, postcode) household always maps to the same 30 * id, independent of which member is registered first, so members share it automatically. 31 */ 32 @Component 33 public class HouseholdIdGenerator { 34 35 /** 36 * Derive the stable household identifier for the given last name and postcode: the first 12 37 * hex characters of the SHA-256 of {@code normalizedLastName + '|' + postcode}. 38 * 39 * @param lastName the household's last name 40 * @param postcode the household's postcode 41 * @return the stable, shared household id 42 */ 43 public String generate(String lastName, String postcode) { 44 String key = canonical(lastName) + "|" + (postcode == null ? "" : postcode); 45 return Sha256.hex(key).substring(0, 12); 46 } 47 48 /** 49 * Canonicalize the last name for household identity: trim, collapse internal runs of 50 * whitespace to a single space and lower-case, so values differing only in casing or 51 * spacing are treated as the same household. 52 */ 53 public String canonical(String value) { 54 return value == null ? "" : value.strip().replaceAll("\\s+", " ").toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT); 55 } 56 } 57

24 import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner; 25 26 /** 27 * Repository class for Owner domain objects All method names are compliant with Spring Data naming 28 * conventions so this interface can easily be extended for Spring Data See here: http://static.springsource.org/spring-data/jpa/docs/current/reference/html/jpa.repositories.html#jpa.query-methods.query-creation 29 * 30 * @author Ken Krebs 31 * @author Juergen Hoeller 32 * @author Sam Brannen 33 * @author Michael Isvy 34 * @author Vitaliy Fedoriv 35 */ 36 public interface OwnerRepository { 37 38 /** 39 * Retrieve Owners from the data store by last name, returning all owners whose last name starts 40 * with the given name. 41 * 42 * @param lastName Value to search for 43 * @return a Collection of matching Owners (or an empty Collection if none 44 * found) 45 */ 46 Collection findByLastName(String lastName) throws DataAccessException; 47 48 Page findByLastName(String lastName, Pageable pageable) throws DataAccessException; 49 50 /** 51 * Retrieve all Owners whose last name equals the given value, ignoring case. 52 * 53 * @param lastName the last name to match (case-insensitively) 54 * @return a Collection of matching Owners (or an empty Collection if none 55 * found) 56 */ 57 Collection findByLastNameIgnoreCase(String lastName) throws DataAccessException; 67 68 /** 69 * Retrieve all Owners stored with the given (normalized) telephone. Used to find the 70 * candidates for an identity-key duplicate check, since owners can only share an identity key when 71 * they share a telephone. 72 * 73 * @param telephone the normalized telephone to look for 74 * @return a Collection of matching Owners (or an empty Collection if none 75 * found) 76 */ 77 Collection findByTelephone(String telephone) throws DataAccessException; 78 79 /** 80 * Report the total number of Owners currently stored. 81 * 82 * @return the count of all owners 83 */ 84 long count() throws DataAccessException; 85 86 /** 87 * Report the number of Owners stored in the given city, matching case-insensitively. 88 * 89 * @param city the city to match (case-insensitively) 90 * @return the count of owners in that city 91 */ 92 long countByCityIgnoreCase(String city) throws DataAccessException; 93 94 /** 95 * Report the number of Owners registered on the given date. 96 * 97 * @param registrationDate the registration date to match 98 * @return the count of owners whose registration date equals the given date 99 */ 100 long countByRegistrationDate(java.time.LocalDate registrationDate) throws DataAccessException; 101 102 103 /** 104 * Save an Owner to the data store, either inserting or updating it. 105 * 106 * @param owner the Owner to save 107 * @see BaseEntity#isNew 108 */ 109 void save(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException; 110 111 /** 112 * Retrieve Owners from the data store, returning all owners 113 * 114 * @return a Collection of Owners (or an empty Collection if none 115 * found) 116 */ 117 Collection findAll() throws DataAccessException; 118 119 Page findAll(Pageable pageable) throws DataAccessException; 120 121 /** 122 * Delete an Owner to the data store by Owner. 123 * 124 * @param owner the Owner to delete 125 * 126 */ 127 void delete(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException; 128 129 130 } 131

The change is implemented and the test suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`).

## What I did

The de-duplication needed to combine two concerns that live in different places, so I split them accordingly:

**1. Persistence check — `OwnerRepository`**
Added `existsByCustomerCode(String)` to the repository interface and its three implementations:
- `SpringDataOwnerRepository` (the active `spring-data-jpa` profile) — Spring Data derives the query automatically.
- `JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl` — a `COUNT` JPQL query.
- `JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl` — a `COUNT(*) ... WHERE customer_code = :customerCode` query (the `customer_code` column exists in every schema).

**2. Code-format / suffix logic — `CustomerCodeGenerator`**
Added a `deduplicate(String customerCode, Predicate<String> isTaken)` method. Since the generator already owns the *shape* of a customer code, the `'-<n>'` collision-suffix format (smallest `n ≥ 2` that is free) belongs here too. It stays pure — it takes a predicate rather than depending on persistence.

**3. Orchestration — `ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner`**
Generates the base code as before, then passes it through `deduplicate(..., ownerRepository::existsByCustomerCode)` before setting it on the owner and saving.

This keeps each unit single-purpose: the repository knows persistence, the generator knows code formatting/collision rules, and the service just wires the two together — no class became a catch-all.
